blocks.text: The Name of Allaah Al-Ghaalib The Predominant is found in one place in the Qur'aan. Allaah says,
And Allah has full power and control over His Affairs, but most of men know not.
The Name An-Naseer The Helper is found in four places,
then know that Allah is your Maula (Patron, Lord, Protector and Supporter, etc.), (what) an Excellent Maula, and (what) an Excellent Helper!
and Allah is Sufficient as a Helper.

and hold fast to Allah [i.e. have confidence in Allah, and depend upon Him in all your affairs] He is your Maula (Patron, Lord, etc.), what an Excellent Maula (Patron, Lord, etc.) and what an Excellent Helper!
But Sufficient is your Lord as a Guide and Helper.
Al-Ghaalib means the One who does as He wills, nothing overcomes Him and none can resist His Rule. No one possesses the ability to repel what He has decreed or prevent what He has concluded.

Qurtubee said, "It is a must for every sane adult to know that Allaah is Al-Ghaalib The unrestrictedly Predominant. Whoever holds on to Him, He will be victorious even if everyone on earth has the same request. Allaah says,
Allah has decreed: "Verily! It is I and My Messengers who shall be the victorious."
Whoever turns away from Allaah and holds onto other than Him will be overcome, in the snares of shaytaan and overturned."

An-Naseer means the One who undertakes to help His servants. He guarantees help for His allies and defends them. Victory cannot come except from Him and cannot be realised except through Him giving it. The one who is victorious is the one that Allaah has aided and granted victory. So there is no helper for the servants except Him and no protector for them except Him.
Allaah says,
And there is no victory except from Allah, the Almighty, the All-Wise.
If Allah helps you, none can overcome you; and if He forsakes you, who is there after Him that can help you?
Allaah has mentioned in multiple places in the Noble Qur'aan His help for His prophets and allies with victory and support. Allaah says,

Verily, We will indeed make victorious Our Messengers and those who believe (in the Oneness of Allah – Islamic Monotheism) in this world's life and on the Day when the witnesses will stand forth, (i.e. Day of Resurrection).
The speech is directed to the believers who establish the rights of faith, outwardly and inwardly, that they will be victorious and have a praiseworthy end in this Life and the Next.

Due to this, the believers who do not strive with their selves to actualise faith or come with the means of victory over the enemies will not achieve victory. Instead their enemies will overpower them due to their sins and shortcomings.

It is also necessary to sincerely turn to the One in whose Hand lies victory. Allaah is the Protector of those who turn to Him, He suffices those who seek His refuge. What a blessed Protector and what a blessed Helper.

keyPoints: The Name Al-Ghaalib is found in one place in the Qur'aan (Yoosuf 12:21), and An-Naseer is found in four places.
Al-Ghaalib means the One who does as He wills; nothing overcomes Him, none can resist His Rule, and none can repel what He has decreed.
Qurtubee said whoever holds on to Allaah will be victorious, and whoever turns away to other than Him will be overcome.
An-Naseer means the One who undertakes to help His servants, guaranteeing help for His allies and defending them; victory comes only from Him.
Allaah's promised victory is for the believers who establish the rights of faith outwardly and inwardly; those who fall short may be overpowered due to their sins.

And there is no victory except from Allah, the Almighty, the All-Wise.

recall.a: The One who does as He wills; nothing overcomes Him and none can resist His Rule or repel what He has decreed.
The One who undertakes to help His servants, guarantees help for His allies and defends them; victory comes only from Him.

recall.q: How many times do Al-Ghaalib and An-Naseer occur in the Qur'aan according to the author?
recall.a: Al-Ghaalib in one place (Yoosuf 12:21) and An-Naseer in four places.

recall.q: Why do some believers not achieve victory over their enemies?
recall.a: Because they do not strive to actualise faith or come with the means of victory, so their enemies overpower them due to their sins and shortcomings.
